## lifecycle

| operation | CLI | MCP | posture | summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`setup`](cards/setup.md) | `setup` | `—` | safe | First-run setup: create local encrypted state, KEK in Keychain, and best-effort registration of the single on-demand curation local-jobs instance when that skill is installed. Fresh installs start LOCAL_ONLY. |
| [`profile.remote_bind`](cards/profile-remote_bind.md) | `profile-remote_bind` | `—` | consequential | Bind an encrypted private-Git backend so your profile can be published for backup and cross-machine use. This does not itself run a recovery drill: separately do one clean-machine recovery with your real recovery key before you rely on this backend to survive machine loss. |
| [`profile.remote_remove`](cards/profile-remote_remove.md) | `profile-remote_remove` | `—` | reversible | Unbind the remote backend and return to LOCAL_ONLY. Local generations are kept. |
| [`key.recover`](cards/key-recover.md) | `key-recover` | `—` | safe | Restore the profile-pack wrapping key from the operator-controlled recovery destination. |
| [`portability.export`](cards/portability-export.md) | `portability-export` | `—` | consequential | Write a passphrase-encrypted (scrypt + AES-256-GCM) portable copy of the profile — subjects, facts, corrections, aliases, generations, and profile-pack keys — for moving to another machine. Sensitive export: requires confirmation. The passphrase is never stored. |
| [`portability.import`](cards/portability-import.md) | `portability-import` | `—` | reversible | Import a passphrase-encrypted portable profile onto this machine. Additive and protective: your operator corrections/confirmations are never overwritten; a wrong passphrase or tampered archive is refused. Profile-pack keys are re-wrapped under this machine's key. |
| [`key.rotate`](cards/key-rotate.md) | `key-rotate` | `—` | consequential | Mint a fresh data-encryption key for the given purpose and destroy the previous one. Anything still encrypted under the old key (for example an already-published profile copy) becomes permanently unreadable — this is the intended 'crypto-shredding' effect of rotating/destroying a key. |
| [`repair`](cards/repair.md) | `repair` | `—` | safe | Verify/replace the runtime payload only. Never touches config, state, backend, or keys. |
| [`uninstall`](cards/uninstall.md) | `uninstall` | `—` | consequential | Remove the installed runtime payload. Profile data/config/keys are untouched. |
